scope: Read-only re-review of the revised exact plan SHA, focusing on the five v1 blockers and whether G0-G7 have independent, executable test oracles. This approves the TC plan only; product/test implementation remains gated on the separate v2 plan review.

v1_blocker_resolution.oracle: The Job DTO and initial DRAFT persist `workflow_version = snapshot.payload.workflow.workflow_id`; the plan fixes the B01 registry ID as `ifpmic-sw-v1`, explicitly distinguishes it from schema_version and profile_version, and requires a literal DTO/DB oracle.

v1_blocker_resolution.result: resolved for the scoped B02 test contract
v1_blocker_resolution.oracle: Catalog fields, snapshot identity/byte uniqueness, append-only eligibility and revocation records, current validity checks, operator-only DB privileges, current_user audit attribution, mock-only CLI grant path, and fail-closed absence of real grant issuance are specified. Synthetic real-grant rows are explicitly test fixtures and cannot be counted as real authority.

Every CreateJob semantic field is retained in immutable ASCII `command_payload_json`; the plan pins the exact version-tagged digest formula and requires independent post-restart payload recovery checks. Digest-only storage is explicitly insufficient.

Project IDs are Unicode scalar identifiers; title/request_text/base_ref/profile_version preserve astral and lone-surrogate strings through ensure_ascii=True semantic JSON persisted as ASCII TEXT, with no raw surrogate sent to PostgreSQL UTF-8. Tests can independently assert exact semantic round-trip and digest.

CSRF is fixed as base64url-no-padding HMAC-SHA256 over the domain-tagged canonical ax_session value using a provisioned private key. It is stable across GETs/restart, changes with session rotation, does not require storing the session token in plaintext, and uses a distinct cursor domain.

testability_review.oidc_and_session: pass: configured protocol fixture, single-use browser-bound state, nonce/PKCE/issuer/audience/azp/signature/time rejection, rotation/logout, stable CSRF and cross-session rejection are independently observable without treating the fixture as corporate SSO
testability_review.authorization_and_operator_boundary: pass: user routes cannot provision owner, membership, delegation, snapshot or approval; isolated PostgreSQL fixtures and the constrained mock-only operator path provide deterministic authorization tests; real grants remain fail-closed pending external authority
testability_review.bridge_and_unicode: pass: raw B01 bytes remain independently pinned and stored; profile labels and user request strings have distinct, explicit lossless storage rules; no Python re-canonicalization is used
testability_review.postgresql_atomicity_and_workspace_fault: pass: real isolated PostgreSQL connections/processes and real temporary filesystem are required for races, rollback, commit uncertainty, reconciler crash windows, marker/symlink/mode checks; mocks are limited to injected boundaries, not acceptance substitutes
testability_review.scope_and_claims: pass: G0-G7 include evidence/recovery and keep B03, B04/B09, all remaining acceptance cases, production environment prerequisites, and full AT-21 explicitly outstanding

remaining_nonblocking_limits: Corporate OIDC registration, production issuer/client/redirect, approved TLS/proxy, real project-role authority, production PostgreSQL/backups, and workspace/storage policy are not supplied by the repository. The plan correctly keeps them as external environment acceptance and requires real startup to fail closed without configuration.
Synthetic OIDC, database fixtures, and local mock profile eligibility validate implemented boundaries only; they cannot close real SSO, real provisioning, B03, B04/B09, or original AT-21.

implementation_gate.reason: The revised plan requires both independent reviewers to approve this same exact SHA before implementation starts.

reviewer_verdict: Approve the independent TC plan for SHA 6bfabb6794b5656a48ebfc1d40e3f007aea3769a19e49a1747ec38b8dd15487a. The five v1 blockers are resolved with independently testable contracts. This review does not authorize implementation on its own or claim real SSO, production approval, or AT-21 acceptance.
